content.intended_use: stabilize_saddle_dynamics: correct the instability of simultaneous gradients in rotational directions

map: Convert the saddle-point condition into projection/monotonicity conditions.
Prove that the distance to any saddle point decreases and the trial-step residual tends to zero.
Use a finite-dimensional cluster-point argument to obtain convergence of the entire sequence.
proofs.omitted_details: The full proof is not stored locally; the map serves only as a locator and cannot certify an independent proof.
proofs.reading_coverage: The original statement and related definitions were checked; the full proof was not independently verified line by line.

assumptions: Q,S are closed and convex; φ is convex–concave and differentiable on Q×S; ||φ_x(z)−φ_x(z′)||≤L||z−z′|| and ||φ_y(z)−φ_y(z′)||≤L||z−z′||; the saddle-point set is nonempty; 0<α<1/L.
statement.objects_and_definitions: A saddle point satisfies φ(x*,y)≤φ(x*,y*)≤φ(x,y*); Eq.(2) defines the iterates.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every feasible initialization, there exists a saddle point (xhat,yhat) to which the entire iterate sequence converges.

unresolved.detail: Separate bounds for phi_x and phi_y with constant L only imply joint T=(phi_x,-phi_y) Lipschitz at most sqrt(2)L. Example phi(x,y)=x²/2+xy: max block constant sqrt(2), but ||[[1,1],[-1,0]]||=(1+sqrt(5))/2>sqrt(2).
unresolved.impact: Do not use the printed step interval 0<alpha<1/L solely from the two block bounds. This example distinguishes the block and joint constants only; it does not determine convergence of extragradient itself.
unresolved.repair: Use a verified joint constant L_T and alpha<1/L_T, or establish the wider step claim separately.
unresolved.target: Theorem 1 assumptions b,c versus proof Eq.(5)

use_restrictions: No independent scientific review has been performed; the material may be used only for pending-review retrieval and research leads, and must not automatically be treated as a certified theorem or used to update the Atlas bracket.

The local example restricts use of the Eq.(5) constant inference; it does not determine the theorem conclusion.
